summary.text: Dione Sims is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 25th District, challenging Rep. Roger Williams. A software quality development director, community organizer and nonprofit founder, she won the March 3, 2026 primary with 60.5% of the vote. She describes herself as a granddaughter of Dr. Opal Lee and says she is running on living wages, public schools and an economy that works for working people.

paragraphs.text: Sims graduated from Southwest High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Texas Wesleyan University in 1989, according to Ballotpedia. FOX 4 describes her degree as a business degree and reports that she started a nonprofit called Unity Unlimited in 2000.

She works in information technology; in her Candidate Connection survey she describes herself as a software quality development director who has led diverse teams of professionals, and as the president and founder of a nonprofit focused on unity, understanding and social justice.

Sims describes herself as the granddaughter of Dr. Opal Lee, whom she calls the Grandmother of Juneteenth. She says she has co-produced the Annual Juneteenth Fort Worth Celebration since 2015 and helped lead the Opal's Walk campaign for national Juneteenth recognition.
She says she has served on several boards, and she lists endorsements from Fort Worth officials and the Fort Worth Association of Federated Women's Club.
FOX 4 reported in January 2026 that she had entered the race. Sims defeated William Marks in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 60.5% to 39.5%.

sources.title: Opal Lee's granddaughter, Dione Sims, enters race for Congress
